clue.text: Article initially consistent with grant to take office

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word consistent is taken

parts.note: to grant is to cede, as in ceding territory

explanation.surface: A rule about how a newspaper article must agree with a funding grant before someone assumes a post.
explanation.definitionFit: To accede is to succeed to a position or throne, which is taking office.

clue.text: Look — a ghost about to disappear!

indicators.note: to disappear means the word for about vanishes from the ghost

parts.note: a spectre is a ghost
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A cry of alarm at a phantom about to vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's aspect is their appearance, the way they look.

clue.text: Gracious king breaks bread with Brit abroad

indicators.note: breaks means the king letter splits the bread word

parts.note: a cob is a round loaf
R is for rex, Latin for king
limey is American slang for a British person

explanation.surface: A kindly monarch shares bread with a British expat.
explanation.walkthrough: COB is a round loaf in Britain; R is the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, like 'good gracious!' — the answer is a London-flavoured one.

clue.text: Morse writer denied vote is put off

indicators.note: denied means the writer's name has the mark for a vote taken away

parts.note: Colin Dexter wrote the Inspector Morse novels
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A crime novelist refused the vote is discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is an Oxford detective series; Colin Dexter wrote it.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to discourage or dissuade them from acting.

clue.text: Official information about posh dwelling-house

indicators.note: about means the official information goes round the posh letter

parts.note: an official communication is a message
U stands for upper-class, hence posh

explanation.surface: A government notice concerning a smart residence.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class usage, so it means posh.
explanation.definitionFit: A messuage is a legal term for a house together with its outbuildings and land.

clue.text: Town converted Asiatic left for the church

parts.note: Eccles is a town near Manchester, famous for its cakes

indicators.note: converted means the letters of Asiatic are changed into a new order, as a convert changes faith

explanation.surface: An Asian man in an English town converts to Christianity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecclesiastical means relating to the church or clergy.

clue.text: American location turns up in atlas

indicators.note: turns means the letters of up in atlas are rearranged

explanation.surface: A US place shows up in a book of maps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' looks like one phrase meaning appears, but 'turns' alone is the anagram signal and 'up' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The state capital of Minnesota is a city in the US, so an American place.

clue.text: Serve Republican British bitter

parts.note: an ace is an unreturnable tennis serve

explanation.surface: Serving a Republican a British bitter beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a literary word for sour or sharp-tasting, harsh in taste.

clue.text: Tees out on eastern sea shown respect

indicators.note: out means the letters of Tees are put out of order

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: The setter, Tees, out on an eastern sea, is honoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TEES as ESTE. Tees is also the setter's own name.
explanation.definitionFit: To be held in high regard is to be admired, so treated with respect.

clue.text: Stories well expressed with changing characters

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings
grammatical speech is correctly phrased

explanation.surface: Tales told well, featuring a shifting cast of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' means letters, not people in the stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to rearranged letters of a word, as in a jumble puzzle.

clue.text: Carthaginian holds educated woman to be strait-laced

indicators.note: holds means the Carthaginian word contains the woman's name

parts.note: Punic means of ancient Carthage
Rita is the heroine of the play and film Educating Rita

explanation.surface: An ancient North African keeps a learned lady prim and proper.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is Willy Russell's play about a hairdresser who studies literature, so the educated woman is RITA.
explanation.definitionFit: Puritanic describes strict moral severity, which is being prim and strait-laced.

clue.text: That is the thing about some in France

indicators.note: about means the thing goes round the French word for some

parts.note: it is the pronoun for a thing
des is French for some

explanation.surface: A clarification of what something in France amounts to.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, abbreviated i.e., is used to mean namely or that is to say.

clue.text: Officer shortly making pass

definitions.meaning: the short form of Colonel, an army officer
a low gap between mountain peaks

explanation.surface: An officer quickly achieving a pass mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for Colonel is also the mountaineer's word for a high gap through a ridge.

clue.text: Sad as the Spanish repeatedly beat Germany back

indicators.note: back means the whole string of pieces is read in reverse order

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
to batter is to beat again and again

explanation.surface: A sporting lament: the Spanish side keep beating Germany in return.
explanation.definitionFit: Something regrettable is unfortunate and to be lamented, hence sad.

clue.text: Almost spear adult beast

indicators.note: almost means the word for spear loses its final letter

parts.note: to impale is to spear or pierce
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A hunter nearly spears a grown animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope, an example of a wild animal.

clue.text: Vitality in a vessel at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or disordered, so the letters of in and vessel are rearranged

explanation.surface: Feeling full of life aboard a ship on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places 'in a vessel at sea' as a scene, but all three words before 'at sea' are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lively and full of energy is vigour, the quality of being lively.

clue.text: See one enigma resolved

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: resolved means the letters of enigma are worked out into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to watch someone crack a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To see something in the mind's eye is to picture or envisage it.

clue.text: Scrutinised bug placed by news boss receiving pressure

indicators.note: placed by means the editor's abbreviation is set beside the bug word
receiving means the bug word takes the pressure letter inside it

parts.note: a bug is an insect
P is the physics symbol for pressure
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: An editor under pressure has a listening device planted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' suggests a hidden microphone, but here it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, so scrutinised is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Blood-stained axe found in Midlands settlement

parts.note: red is the colour of something blood-stained
to axe something is to ditch or scrap it

explanation.surface: A murder weapon turns up in an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: REDDITCH is a town in Worcestershire, in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in Worcestershire, in central England, is a Midlands settlement.

clue.text: See problem having one brought into heaven

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: brought into means the numeral is placed inside the word for a problem

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Solving one problem gets you into paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; ELY is the usual crossword one.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Elysian fields are the paradise of the blessed dead.

clue.text: Place in window for trumpet

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for place goes inside the window word

parts.note: a sash is a sliding window frame
Pl is the street-name abbreviation for Place

explanation.surface: Someone puts a trumpet on the window sill.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet news is to publicise it loudly, as a newspaper does with a front-page story.

clue.text: Extravagant American leaving Sunshine State

indicators.note: leaving means the abbreviation for American departs from the state

parts.note: the Sunshine State is the nickname of Florida

explanation.surface: A flamboyant American moving out of Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: Florid style is over-ornate and showy, so extravagant.

clue.text: Aftershock — in a word — seen in Madeira?

definitions.text: Aftershock — in a word — seen in Madeira?

parts.words: Aftershock — in a word — seen in Madeira?
parts.note: split the single word differently: AFTERS is a pudding and HOCK is a German white, and Madeira is one such sweet fortified drink

explanation.surface: A tremor after an earthquake on the Portuguese island of Madeira.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a word' tells you to read the one word Aftershock as two: afters (British slang for pudding) and hock (a Rhine wine).
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a sweet fortified drink served with or after pudding, the question mark flagging an example.

clue.text: Cheerio having to lose good old statesman

indicators.note: to lose means the letter for good is dropped from the farewell

parts.note: so long is a casual goodbye, like cheerio

explanation.surface: Bidding farewell to a fine elder politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheerio is a British informal goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Solon was the lawgiver of ancient Athens, an early statesman.

clue.text: Energy shown by man climbing to escape

indicators.note: climbing means the energy letter and the man's name together read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
Dave is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man shows the energy to climb his way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses EDAVE as a whole in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to dodge or avoid, getting away from something.

clue.text: Slippery character getting into free love

indicators.note: getting into means the letters sit inside the words free love

explanation.surface: A shifty type taking up with the permissive society.
explanation.definitionFit: This fish is famously hard to grip, the source of the phrase about a slippery customer.

clue.text: Duke in hat sees señorita's wiggle

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for duke goes inside the hat word

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A nobleman in headgear eyes a Spanish girl's wiggle.
explanation.definitionFit: The wavy mark over the Spanish ñ, as in the word for miss, looks like a little wiggle.

clue.text: Privilege to receive current letter

indicators.note: to receive means the privilege word takes the abbreviation for current inside it

parts.note: a charter grants a privilege or right
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A right to be sent the latest letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A written symbol of the alphabet is called a character, as in typography.

clue.text: Straight home in divine surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the word for divine goes around the word for home

parts.note: holy means sacred or divine
a nest is a home, as in a family nest

explanation.surface: Going straight home within a sacred setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken as an adverb, it means frankly or truthfully, giving it to you straight.

clue.text: We would accept old age having stuck together

indicators.note: accept means the contraction takes the word for old age inside it

parts.note: we'd is the contraction of we would
eld is an archaic word for old age

explanation.surface: A couple who would embrace growing old and stay together.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal pieces fused by heat are joined, i.e. fixed together.
